offence_severity: Death (Section 302) with minimum/maximum punishment as per IPC
physical_harm: Incised wounds and internal injuries leading to neurogenic and hemorrhagic shock
number_of_offences: Four counts charged, three finally upheld
premeditation_planning: Yes, accused no. 1 caused the deceased to be killed and engaged accused no. 2 and 4 as contract killers
key_evidence_accepted: The deposition of PW-21, a 13-year-old servant brought by accused no. 1, was accepted as reliable. His statement that accused no. 2 attacked the deceased with a knife was corroborated by the recovery of the knife from accused no. 2. The court also noted that accused no. 1 had a scuffle with the deceased, as evidenced by her hair being found in her grip during investigation.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the child witness PW-21 as credible, noting that he had no motive to falsely implicate the accused, was taken care of by accused no. 1, and had no ulterior motive. His testimony was not discarded despite his association with the police, and his statement was corroborated by the recovery of the knife from accused no. 2.
trial_duration: The trial judgment was delivered on 17.09.2010 by the High Court of Chhattisgarh at Bilaspur, and the Supreme Court decision was on 21 August 2014.
legal_representation: For the Appellant: P.C. Agrawala, Dr. Rajesh Pandey, Mahesh Pandey, Priyanka Pandey, Mridula Ray Bhardwaj, Revathy Raghavan, Vidya Dhar Gaur; For the Respondent: Atul Jha, Sandeep Jha, Dharmendra Kumar Sinha
investigation_status: FIR registered on 25.11.2003, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction under Section 302 r/w Section 34 and Section 1208, IPC; High Court: Confirmed the conviction; Supreme Court: Dismissed the appeals of accused no. 1, 2 and 4 and allowed the appeal of accused no. 3
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that accused no. 1 hired contract killers accused no. 2 and 4 to kill her daughter-in-law (deceased) due to domestic disputes. The child witness PW-21, who was brought up by accused no. 1, provided testimony that accused no. 2 and 4 attacked the deceased with a knife, and the knife was recovered from accused no. 2. The prosecution also highlighted the motive of accused no. 1 to hinder the marriage of her son.
defence_argument: The defence argued that accused no. 3 (Mahesh) did not play any role in the crime, as there was no evidence of his involvement, no weapon or property connected with the crime was seized from him, and he was merely seen standing outside the house. The defence also questioned the reliability of the child witness PW-21, suggesting he might have been tutored by the police.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that common intention and conspiracy are matters of inference, and if any benefit of doubt arises, it must go to the accused. The Court also emphasized the need for corroboration of the testimony of a child witness in cases where the accused are strangers to the witness.
precedent_relied_upon: Subash and Shiv Kumar Vs. State of UP. (1987) 3 SCC 331; Mohd. Abdul Hafeez Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh AIR 1983 SC 367; Budhsen and Anr. Vs. State of UP. (1970) 2 SCC 128; Suresh Sakharam Nangare Vs. State of Maharashtra (2012) 9 SCC 249; Jai Bhagwan Vs. State of Haryana AIR 1999 SC 1083; Ramashish Yadav Vs. State of Bihar (1999) 8 SCC 555; Baliya v. State of M.P. (2012) 9 SCC 696
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed as the Court upheld the conviction of accused no. 1, 2, and 4 under Section 302 r/w Section 34 and 1208 of the IPC, considering the evidence of the child witness and the corroborating knife recovery. Accused no. 3 was acquitted due to lack of evidence of his involvement.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The Court considered that the child witness PW-21 was brought up by accused no. 1, who took care of him, sent him to school, and provided him with food and residence, which made it unlikely for him to falsely implicate anyone.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The Court noted that accused no. 2 and 4 had a single mission to kill the deceased, and there was no evidence of their previous animosity with the deceased, indicating a premeditated act.
other_sentence_order: The Court acquitted accused no. 3 and discharged his bail bonds and sureties. It also emphasized the need for corroboration of child witness testimony and the importance of fair identification procedures.
